eventMetadata.context_description: As Lagos transitions into its rainy season—forecast by NiMet's 2026 outlook to be longer than normal with warmer overall temperatures—short-term models from AccuWeather project May highs averaging 31–33°C, consistent with historical May peaks around 32°C. Inherent forecast uncertainty persists due to convective activity and steering winds, with NiMet daily bulletins and updated ECMWF ensembles expected to refine trader consensus before May 15 resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Following the rapid dissipation of a severe cold front that lashed Cape Town with heavy rainfall, gale-force winds, and flooding through May 13, South African Weather Service (SAWS) guidance points to clearing skies and milder autumn conditions on May 15, anchoring trader-implied odds tightly around 19–22°C outcomes. Ensemble forecasts from models like ECMWF proxies (yr.no at 19°C max) and GFS-influenced runs (weather.com at 20°C) reflect post-frontal high-pressure ridging and seasonal norms of ~20°C May highs, but with uncertainty from variable cloud cover, light southerly winds (4 m/s), and low precipitation risk (0–8%). Warmer 24°C+ sentiment at 25.5% weighs above-normal temperature outlooks, while sub-20°C shares account for potential marine layer persistence; fresh SAWS advisories and model updates today could shift the balance.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest extended outlook, updated May 13, forecasts Metro Manila highs of 35°C on May 15 amid partly cloudy skies, isolated thunderstorms from a nearby low pressure area, and increasing rain chances to 70%, anchoring trader consensus with equal implied probabilities near 34-36°C at NAIA station—the market's resolution source. Differentiating factors include potential midday cloud breaks boosting solar insolation for 36-37°C spikes, versus afternoon sea breeze or convection capping at 33-34°C, amplified by urban heat island effects at the airport. Historical May averages hover at 34°C, but recent days hit 36.7°C at nearby Science Garden amid high heat indices over 42°C. Daily PAGASA updates and global model runs (GFS, ECMWF) overnight could refine peak timing uncertainties.
